title: RBI Advisory — Beware of Fraudulent Calls and Messages
text: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has issued multiple advisories warning customers that RBI never contacts individuals to ask for personal or banking details, OTPs, PINs, or account numbers. RBI does not issue offers of loans, lottery winnings, or prizes. Any call or message claiming to be from RBI and asking for personal financial information is fraudulent. The RBI also clarifies that banks in India follow a strict policy of never asking customers for their internet banking passwords, OTPs, CVV numbers, or card expiry dates over phone or SMS. If your bank genuinely needs to verify your KYC, they will ask you to visit the branch or use the official app — they will never ask for sensitive credentials remotely. KYC (Know Your Customer) updates do not require sharing OTP. The RBI advises: (1) Never share OTP, PIN, password, or card details with anyone. (2) Banks never ask for these over calls or SMS. (3) When in doubt, call your bank's official helpline number on the back of your card. (4) Report fraud at 1930 (National Cyber Crime helpline) or cybercrime.gov.in.
